You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/kvm/vmx/pmu_intel.c`**
   - Introduced a new variable `hw_idx` to store the hardware index of the performance event.
   - Added a comment explaining that a negative index indicates the event isn't mapped to a physical counter in the host due to contention.
   - Modified the condition that checks if the performance event's index (`hw_idx`) is different from the PMC's index (`pmc->idx`). The new condition also checks if `hw_idx` is greater than -1 before updating `pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the file are related to addressing a potential out-of-bounds access issue when handling performance events in the KVM PMU (Performance Monitoring Unit). The change ensures that the `host_cross_mapped_mask` is only updated with valid hardware indices, preventing the use of a negative index that could occur in scenarios of multiplexing and contention. This fix is a direct response to the bug identified in the previous commit, enhancing the robustness of the PMU handling in the KVM environment.

1. explain how the bug occurs, including all code statements that are most likely to lead to the bug and why. 
2. explain how the bug is fixed, including code statements fixing the bug and why. 

You must include one or more code statements in point 1 and 2.
Code statements included in point 1 should be as brief as possible, only include the ones that are most related to the root cause and  the number of code statements may not exceed 3.


Here is the commit message:
KVM: x86/pmu: Avoid setting BIT_ULL(-1) to
 pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask

In the extreme case of host counters multiplexing and contention, the
perf_event requested by the guest's pebs counter is not allocated to any
actual physical counter, in which case hw.idx is bookkept as -1,
resulting in an out-of-bounds access to host_cross_mapped_mask.

Fixes: 854250329c02 ("KVM: x86/pmu: Disable guest PEBS temporarily in two rare situations")
Signed-off-by: Like Xu <likexu@tencent.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220831085328.45489-2-likexu@tencent.com
[sean: expand comment to explain how a negative idx can be encountered]
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs when the performance event requested by the guest's PEBS (Precise Event-Based Sampling) counter is not allocated to any actual physical counter, resulting in the hardware index (`hw.idx`) being set to -1. This negative index leads to an out-of-bounds access when attempting to set the `host_cross_mapped_mask`, which can cause undefined behavior or crashes.

Here is the patch:
 
 void intel_pmu_cross_mapped_check(struct kvm_pmu *pmu)
 {
 	struct kvm_pmc *pmc = NULL;
-	int bit;
+	int bit, hw_idx;
 
 	for_each_set_bit(bit, (unsigned long *)&pmu->global_ctrl,
 			 X86_PMC_IDX_MAX) {
 		pmc = intel_pmc_idx_to_pmc(pmu, bit);
 
 		if (!pmc || !pmc_speculative_in_use(pmc) ||
-		    !intel_pmc_is_enabled(pmc))
+		    !intel_pmc_is_enabled(pmc) || !pmc->perf_event)
 			continue;
 
-		if (pmc->perf_event && pmc->idx != pmc->perf_event->hw.idx) {
-			pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask |=
-				BIT_ULL(pmc->perf_event->hw.idx);
-		}
+		/*
+		 * A negative index indicates the event isn't mapped to a
+		 * physical counter in the host, e.g. due to contention.
+		 */
+		hw_idx = pmc->perf_event->hw.idx;
+		if (hw_idx != pmc->idx && hw_idx > -1)
+			pmu->host_cross_mapped_mask |= BIT_ULL(hw_idx);
 	}
 }

Reason: The code snippet checks if `pmc` is valid and if `pmc->idx` is not equal to `pmc->perf_event->hw.idx` before attempting to set the `host_cross_mapped_mask`. However, it does not explicitly check if `pmc->perf_event->hw.idx` is a valid index (i.e., not -1) before using it in the bitwise operation. If `pmc->perf_event->hw.idx` is -1, this will lead to an out-of-bounds access when attempting to set the `host_cross_mapped_mask`, which aligns with the described bug.
